newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said property prices were too high and speculative activities had gone too far. But he refused to promise to take measures to bring down property prices for the time being.
-- Hongkong Bank said China had not expressed any intention of buying a stake in Hang Seng Bank.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) had had a good beginning and the central government had sent very positive messages to Hong Kong people.
-- WEN WEI PO -- The SAR government presented the Grand Bauhinia medal to 12 prominent Hong Kong figures for their contributions to the territory's development.

-- MING PAO -- About 100 illegal immigrant children will go go to the immigration department to apply for Hong Kong identity cards because, according to the Basic Law, they can now become Hong Kong citizens since the SAR had been established.

-- SING TAO -- Chinese leaders will gather in the seaside city of Beidaihe to prepare for the 15th Communist Party general conference. According to sources, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji will replace Li Peng as Premier, while Li will become Vice President

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Former Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten could be coming back to Hong Kong within the year to front a television series on Asia. Patten will further discuss the deal in London later this month.
-- Thailand's decision yesterday to float its currency pushed the baht to a record low against the U.S. dollar and sent shockwaves through other Asian markets.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China Resources Holding is borrowing US$250 million to finance debt and boost its working capital. The mainland group has already mandated a group of banks as arrangers.
